text:
Code
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(leaflet)
library(terra)
library(here)

source(here("R", "functions.R"))
derived <- here(cfg$paths$derived)

line    <- load_transect()
aoi     <- load_aoi()
windows <- load_windows()
nlcd    <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "nlcd_windows.csv"))
classes <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "nlcd_window_classes.csv"))
lc      <- rast(here(cfg$nlcd$dir, sprintf("LndCov_%d.tif", cfg$nlcd$year)))

windows <- left_join(windows, nlcd, by = c("window", "u_start_km", "u_end_km", "u_mid_km", "area_km2"))

# Grouped cover, ordered from most to least urban; colors follow the NLCD legend
cover_cols <- c(
  developed      = "#eb0000",
  developed_open = "#dec5c5",
  barren         = "#b3ac9f",
  agriculture    = "#dcd939",
  shrub_grass    = "#ccb879",
  forest         = "#38814e",
  wetland        = "#b8d9eb",
  water          = "#466b9f"
)
cover_labels <- c(
  developed = "Developed (low to high)", developed_open = "Developed, open space",
  barren = "Barren", agriculture = "Agriculture", shrub_grass = "Shrub and grassland",
  forest = "Forest", wetland = "Wetland", water = "Water"
)

title: Urban to Forest Gradient
text:
Purpose
A first look at how land use changes from downtown Richmond to Pocahontas State Park. The study area is cut into non-overlapping 1 km windows along the transect, each spanning the full 4 km buffer width, and each window is summarized from the Annual NLCD 2025 land cover and fractional impervious surface layers (30 m).








Step
Script
Output




5. Transect windows
R/04_transect_windows.R
data/derived/transect_windows.gpkg


6. NLCD download and window summaries
R/05_nlcd.R
data/raw/nlcd/*.tif, data/derived/nlcd_windows.csv, nlcd_window_classes.csv



NLCD is kept on its native grid (EPSG:5070). Windows are projected to it and summarized with exactextractr, which weights each 30 m cell by the fraction of it inside the window.

title: Urban to Forest Gradient
text:
Gradient
Share of each window in each grouped cover type, from Richmond (left) to Pocahontas State Park (right).


Code
cover_long <- nlcd |>
  select(window, u_mid_km, ends_with("_pct")) |>
  pivot_longer(ends_with("_pct"), names_to = "cover", values_to = "pct") |>
  mutate(cover = factor(sub("_pct$", "", cover), levels = names(cover_cols)))

ggplot(cover_long, aes(u_mid_km, pct, fill = cover)) +
  geom_col(width = cfg$windows$length_km * 0.95) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cover_cols, labels = cover_labels, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 25, 5), expand = expansion(add = 0.3)) +
  labs(x = "Distance from Richmond (km)", y = "Share of window (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())









Mean fractional impervious surface and forest cover per window. Shaded bands are ± 1 SD of impervious surface among the 30 m cells in each window.


Code
grad <- nlcd |>
  transmute(u_mid_km,
            `Impervious surface` = imperv_mean,
            Forest = forest_pct,
            lo = pmax(imperv_mean - imperv_sd, 0),
            hi = imperv_mean + imperv_sd) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`Impervious surface`, Forest), names_to = "measure", values_to = "pct")

ggplot(grad, aes(u_mid_km, pct, colour = measure)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = filter(grad, measure == "Impervious surface"),
              aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80", colour = NA, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`Impervious surface` = "#5e3c99", Forest = "#38814e"),
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 25, 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Distance from Richmond (km)", y = "Percent") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

title: Urban to Forest Gradient
text:
Notes

Data: Annual NLCD Collection 1, 2025 land cover (LndCov) and fractional impervious surface (FctImp), read for the AOI bounding box from the USGS web coverage service (https://dmsdata.cr.usgs.gov/geoserver). No resampling or reprojection of the rasters.
Developed combines NLCD classes 22–24 (low, medium, high intensity). Developed open space (21) is mostly lawns, parks, and road verges and is kept separate. Forest is classes 41–43; wetland is 90 and 95.
Windows are not replicated samples. Adjacent windows are spatially autocorrelated, so the curves describe the gradient but should not be treated as 25 independent observations.
The 4 km width averages across very different ground on either side of the line (e.g. the James River crossing near 5–7 km). A narrower center band would test how much that matters.

Code
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(leaflet)
library(yaml)
library(here)

cfg <- read_yaml(here("config.yml"))
derived <- here(cfg$paths$derived)

pts   <- st_read(file.path(derived, "aoi.gpkg"), layer = "transect_points", quiet = TRUE)
line  <- st_read(file.path(derived, "aoi.gpkg"), layer = "transect_line",   quiet = TRUE)
aoi   <- st_read(file.path(derived, "aoi.gpkg"), layer = "aoi",             quiet = TRUE)
tiles <- st_read(file.path(derived, "tiles_needed.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)

# Status is checked at render time; tile paths are relative to the project root
tiles$converted <- file.exists(here(tiles$tif_path))
tiles$state <- case_when(
  tiles$converted          ~ "converted",
  tiles$status == "local"  ~ "local (not converted)",
  TRUE                     ~ "missing (download needed)"
)
state_cols <- c("converted" = "#1b9e77",
                "local (not converted)" = "#7570b3",
                "missing (download needed)" = "#d95f02")

title: Study Area and Orthoimagery
text:
Purpose
This project uses 2025 Virginia Base Mapping Program (VBMP) orthoimagery along a transect from industrial Richmond to Pocahontas State Park. The statewide imagery is distributed as MrSID tiles. Only the tiles that overlap the study area are converted to GeoTIFF and combined into a single virtual mosaic.








Step
Script
Output




1. Build transect and buffer
R/01_build_aoi.R
data/derived/aoi.gpkg


2. Select intersecting tiles
R/02_select_tiles.R
data/derived/tiles_needed.{gpkg,csv}


3. Convert MrSID to GeoTIFF
python/convert_mrsid.py (QGIS Python console)
data/geotiff/*.tif


4. Virtual mosaic
R/03_build_vrt.R
data/derived/ortho_12in.vrt, ortho_12in_preview.tif



All parameters live in config.yml. Analysis scripts load the imagery with load_ortho() from R/functions.R, which returns the mosaic limited to the study area without copying any data.

title: Study Area and Orthoimagery
text:
Notes

Imagery source: VBMP 2025 12-inch orthoimagery (Sanborn Map Company, flown February to March 2025), distributed by the Virginia Geographic Information Network (VGIN). The MrSID versions are RGB only. The near-infrared band is only in the TIFF deliverables.
Tile layout: each 12-inch tile is 5,000 × 5,000 px at 1 ft, covering 5,000 × 5,000 ft. Tile names follow DO_S13_<section>_<quarter>.2025.
MrSID decoding: the MrSID GDAL driver only loads inside the QGIS application (macOS code-signing blocks it from the command line), so conversion runs in the QGIS Python console.
Mosaic edges: the VRT has no nodata value. Areas outside the tiles read as 0 in all three bands; all such areas lie outside the study area.
